items.title: Gucci's China-made sneakers in focus as Kering stock sits 41.82% below 52-week high
items.summary: German financial wire ties Gucci's new 'Made in China' Drip and Primavera slip-on sneakers to investor unease, noting Kering stock traded at EUR 206.05 on Oct 8, down 41.8% from its 52-week high, with H1 2026 group net income down 60% and Gucci revenue down 5%. Goldman Sachs initiated coverage Oct 4 at Neutral with a EUR 250 target, citing execution risk.

items.title: Luca de Meo: 'recovery signals from Gucci', calls Balenciaga creative transition 'pretty extreme'
items.summary: Kering CEO Luca de Meo told WWD he sees early recovery signals at Gucci and is restructuring the group around creative studios, saying distribution, marketing, product and collections are all being 'realigned'. He separately called the Balenciaga handover from Demna to Pierpaolo Piccioli 'pretty extreme' and flagged the industry's 6-8 month ideation-to-shelf cycle as too slow versus competitors.

items.title: Weak autumn for luxury: China weighs on the sector, US remains resilient
items.summary: Italian trade outlet's autumn luxury-sector round-up flags China demand as the continuing drag across the industry, including Gucci, while describing the US as comparatively resilient; notes Kering reports Q3 results Oct 22 with Barclays modeling group organic revenue down 1.5% and Gucci down 6%.

items.title: Gucci UK: sales and profits down in 2025 filing
items.summary: Newly filed UK accounts show Gucci's British unit posted a 28.4% revenue decline to GBP 105.4 million and operating profit of just GBP 3.9 million amid weaker demand, with the company describing itself as 'satisfied' with performance in a difficult market context.

items.title: Drip sneaker continues to raise questions about Gucci and 'Made in Italy'
items.summary: Italian trade outlet LaConceria revisits the Gucci Drip sneaker's 'Made in China' label a week after launch, arguing the decision keeps generating reputational friction for Kering's flagship brand and tests how much the 'Made in Italy' identity still matters to luxury buyers.

items.source: Instagram (public comments on Gucci Primavera AI campaign)
items.title: Instagram backlash continues over Gucci's AI-generated Primavera campaign images
items.summary: Public comment threads on Gucci's Instagram remain active days after the AI-generated 'Primavera' campaign images dropped, with recurring complaints that a brand charging luxury prices should not rely on 'AI slop'; one widely echoed comment compared the practice to being 'no different than Zara.' A smaller set of commenters defended the aesthetic as 'stunning' and era-appropriate.

items.title: Fashion forum members split on Gucci SS2027 Milan show, menswear-heavy focus criticized
items.summary: In an active 9-page thread, fashion-enthusiast forum members are predominantly critical of Demna's SS2027 Gucci presentation, with one post calling it 'a tragedy' and 'an absolute lack of vision,' and several objecting that womenswear was sidelined ('we've given up on womenswear it seems'). A smaller number of posters praised the casting and called it 'a step in the right direction.' Reactions per post range from single digits to 20+.
